 RBI Likely to Hike Repo Rate by 0.50% Amid Rising Inflation: Report
 New Delhi: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to increase the repo rate by 25 basis points (bps) in both its December and February monetary policy reviews. This comes as headline inflation has surpassed the RBI's upper tolerance limit of 6% for the first time in the new series.
 According to a report by Choice Institutional Equities, the repo rate, currently at 5.5%, is projected to reach approximately 6.25%. India's retail inflation, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), jumped to 6.1% in October from 5.5% in September, exceeding the 6% ceiling. This indicates that inflation is no longer confined to food items alone.
 Core inflation has also firmed up to 4.6% from 4.5%, with nearly two-thirds of household expenses now rising faster than the RBI's target midpoint. Food and beverage inflation accelerated to 8.5%, with the food index hitting a new high of 8.9%. Specifically, vegetable prices surged by 10.9%.
 Dairy products are also seeing significant price hikes, with milk, eggs, and dairy inflation reaching 5.6%. Major cooperatives like Amul, Mother Dairy, and Nandini have repeatedly increased prices, pushing the average retail milk price to around Rs 63 per litre from Rs 59 in March.
 Both rural and urban inflation have risen sharply, with urban inflation now climbing faster as the impact of food price increases reaches cities through processed products, dining out, and transport. Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation also accelerated to 12.3%, almost double the CPI, driven by a 32.8% increase in fuel and power costs. This suggests that further price increases for consumers are likely. The report emphasizes that the breach in inflation targets will push the RBI to take decisive action.
